clue.text: See 17
Smut in Springfield not unknown?

indicators.note: not says the following letter is left out of the singer's first name

parts.note: Dusty Springfield was a British pop singer of the 1960s
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns, alongside X and Z

explanation.surface: A question about some scandal or filth turning up in an American town called Springfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Springfield reads as a place but stands for the singer Dusty Springfield; 'not' removes Y from her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut can mean specks of soot or grime, a synonym for fine dirty particles.

clue.text: Lovers' tiff ending, somewhat tense

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A quarrel between lovers comes to an end, though things stay a little strained.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to tense is to become rigid, a synonym of the verb in the solution.

clue.text: Covering with wood, temperature in damaged roof ain't safe

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the jumbled letters
damaged signals that the letters of roof ain't safe are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that heat in a ruined roof makes it unsafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Planting trees over land covers it with woodland, which is what this forestry term names.

clue.text: Barbie's partner wears fashionable second layers

indicators.note: wears pictures the doll inside the clothing-like outer letters, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: chic means stylish or fashionable
Ken is the boyfriend doll of Barbie

explanation.surface: Ken the doll dresses in trendy clothes, worn in layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' looks like clothing but means hens, birds that lay eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens are kept as egg producers, so they are layers in farming terms.

clue.text: From kitchen, a choice snack

indicators.note: From says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the following words

explanation.surface: Something tasty to nibble picked out of the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla chip topped with cheese is a popular Mexican-style snack.

clue.text: Fake priest will ignore article

indicators.note: will ignore says the article is left out of the priest's word

parts.note: a shaman is a priest or healer in tribal religions
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A bogus cleric skips over a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fake is a pretence or imitation, a synonym of the answer as noun or adjective.

clue.text: Selfish person? More difficult to keep nothing

indicators.note: to keep says the zero is held inside the comparative word

parts.note: harder means more difficult
O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone self-centred finds it tougher to have nothing to call their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a stockpiler is a kind of selfish person.
explanation.definitionFit: One who stockpiles goods and keeps them back from others can be seen as greedy.

clue.text: Peak of affair — one might blow it

parts.note: an affair is a business or matter
a horn is an instrument you blow

explanation.surface: The high point of a romance, one you might ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peak of affair' reads as one phrase, but 'Peak' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous Alpine mountain on the Swiss-Italian border, an example of a peak.

clue.text: Tin with one very strong smell

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
I is the Roman numeral one
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud or strong

explanation.surface: A tin can with a powerful odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A short inhaled breath to catch a scent, or a faint whiff, is a smell.

clue.text: An insect's awfully persistent

indicators.note: awfully signals that the letters of an insect's are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A bug that will not go away is dreadfully pestering.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unceasing and never letting up is persistent.

clue.text: I'll sit on sofa going crazy, accepting SAGE's ultimate protective measure

indicators.note: accepting says the jumble takes in one more letter
going crazy signals that the letters of I'll sit on sofa are scrambled
ultimate picks the last letter of the advisory body's name

explanation.surface: A pandemic-era lockdown complaint: sitting on the sofa driving me mad, following the scientific advisers' final advice.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGE is the UK government's Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies, prominent during Covid; its last letter E goes into the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping away from others while infectious was a Covid precaution to protect the public.

clue.text: Early intelligence for English king: northern flier approaching border

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
an owl is a bird, a flier
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: Advance information about an English monarch: a northern bird is nearing the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing about events beforehand is advance information, intelligence gained early.

clue.text: Lucky escape as criminal chases love

indicators.note: criminal signals that the letters of chases love are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A narrow getaway while a crook runs after romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a narrow escape from disaster or injury.

clue.text: Put down post for tourist landmark

parts.note: to land is to put down, as an aircraft
to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: Instructions to set down a signpost at a sightseeing spot.
explanation.walkthrough: LAND'S END is the westernmost tip of Cornwall in England, a popular tourist spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cornish headland is a famous visitor attraction, an example of a tourist landmark.

clue.text: One man in a boat turned back to find old address

indicators.note: turned back says the man's name is read from end to start

parts.note: Harris is one of the trio in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat

explanation.surface: A lone sailor rows back to locate a former home address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' is not a home but a form of address: a dated way to speak to a man of lower rank.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic term of address was used, often contemptuously, to men or boys.

clue.text: Carry weapons with sleeves rolled up, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals the answer sounds like the phrase described

parts.note: with sleeves rolled up your forearms are uncovered, bare

explanation.surface: Armed men getting ready for action with their sleeves pushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, familiar from the US Second Amendment, means to carry weapons.

clue.text: Clan dissociating, sadly — to observe this?

definitions.text: Clan dissociating, sadly — to observe this?

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters of clan dissociating are rearranged, as if in a sorry state

explanation.surface: A family drifting apart, regrettably, as they keep a pandemic rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: families kept apart during Covid were following this rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping apart from others was a Covid rule, and a clan dissociating is doing exactly that.

clue.text: Church member meeting Queen a hit with the ladies?

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher for the Queen

explanation.surface: A churchgoer meets the Queen and wins over the women.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of great appeal who wins over women is a smooth, attractive charmer type.

clue.text: Refined revolutionary plot being broadcast

indicators.note: revolutionary says the plot word is turned around

parts.note: a plot of garden is a bed
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A sophisticated rebel scheme is being transmitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a stylish, suave and polished manner, synonymous with refined.

clue.text: Body found in A&E ward finally collected

indicators.note: found in says the body word sits inside the hospital department's letters

parts.note: A&E, accident and emergency, gives the letters A and E
a mass is a body of matter

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of ward

explanation.surface: A corpse discovered in a hospital casualty ward was eventually removed.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gathered things into a heap is to have accumulated or collected them.

clue.text: Jacks lost after playing bowls?

parts.note: legend says Drake finished his game of bowls before sailing out to beat the Spanish fleet, so its sailors (jacks, jack tars) lost after he played

explanation.surface: In bowls the jack is the small target ball; here they go missing after a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1588 Sir Francis Drake is said to have finished his game of bowls at Plymouth before defeating the invading Spanish fleet; 'Jacks' are sailors, not the target balls.
explanation.definitionFit: The invasion fleet of 1588 was defeated, so its sailors were the losers after the famous bowls game.

clue.text: One loathes half-hearted madman?

indicators.note: half-hearted says the middle double letter loses half, one of the pair

parts.note: the Mad Hatter is the madman of Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Someone who detests a lukewarm lunatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who loathes something is someone who feels hatred toward it.

clue.text: Support Remain

definitions.meaning: a prop or brace, as in a corset or a ship's rope
to stop on somewhere rather than leave

explanation.surface: A slogan from the Brexit referendum, backing the Remain side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a supporting prop and to linger or not leave.

clue.text: Almost get rid of church carpet

indicators.note: Almost says the final letter is dropped from the word for getting rid of

parts.note: to axe something is to get rid of it
a minster is a large church

explanation.surface: A near decision to throw out the church's floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a type of woven carpet named after the Devon town where it was first made.

clue.text: Six-footer not about to be small figure?

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation for about is removed

parts.note: an insect has six legs, so is a six-footer
C, circa, is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A very tall person who is not quite a little character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person but means a creature with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small picture or diagram set inside a larger one is a small figure on a page.

clue.text: Upset real toff

indicators.note: Upset signals that the letters of real are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A genuine posh person is offended.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman ranking above a viscount is an example of an aristocratic toff.

clue.text: Christmas, now!

definitions.meaning: a day for giving gifts, read cryptically
the current era, the time we live in

explanation.surface: An exclamation demanding the festivities begin immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a day of gifts; as a phrase it means contemporary times.
